# K-of-n routing, co-errors and crowded-theme measurement

**Recommendation: reject k-of-n for v1.** No tested setting improves estimated recall while meeting the unchanged text precision point. The image-free ablation also has no qualifying setting. V1, its tie order, worked examples and settled liveness thresholds remain unchanged; images stay out entirely, including shadow mode.

## Scope and corrections

The requested “same population and estimator” comparison reproduces the archived text benchmark exactly, including its known missing-URI definition bug. That is a historical comparison, not renewed evidence that missing metadata means copying. The separate nonempty-URI sensitivity removes that credit and recomputes the same estimator; no missing URI/social/image value can fire any scorer signal. No new semantic labels are inferred from images or social equality.

There is no approved production image threshold. This offline study uses the strictest previously measured Hamming point, zero; it does not enable images or shadow processing. “Error” in the legacy-estimator table means expected wrong-route credit under that estimator, including unsupported pairs scored zero, not an independently confirmed false match. The direct-D check is shown separately. The crowding/correlation hypothesis is not uniformly confirmed, so the results do not claim it is.

The study uses the same 2956 actual launches, ordered by slot/signature. Every room is explicitly assumed live, as in text calibration; no reserve, idle, volume or pool states are fabricated. These are conditional metadata benchmark estimates, not production precision/recall. No pre-window rooms, synthetic launches, new network requests or image decoding are introduced. Metadata and real-image hashes are the checked-in observations; source file hashes are in the JSON report.

The only semantic label file is `labels_assistant.csv`, exactly as requested. No image-aware or new social labels are added. Equal folded identity or URI follows the archival positive definition; direct S/D labels score one/zero; U/unlabelled pairs use their strongest text-stratum rate. Pairs without a supported stratum or direct label score zero. That last rule is estimator coverage, not proof of a false route. Recall uses the fixed text-findable expected-copy population, not newly discovered social/image-only copies.

## Signals and deterministic benchmark policy

| vote | predicate |
|---|---|
| name_equal | Nonempty folded name keys equal. A short name can cast a vote; the existing name-only v1 route still requires its original minimum length. |
| symbol_equal | Nonempty folded symbol keys equal. |
| x_post | A nonempty specific X status ID matches, using the social audit’s cached JSON and normalisation. Uncapped in this separate experiment. |
| image_h0 | Both real 64-bit pHashes exist and have Hamming distance ≤ 0. Missing hashes never match, including missing against missing. |
| fuzzy_name | Name-token Jaccard ≥ 0.5, with a shared token of length ≥ 4. It can overlap exact-name equality. |
| symbol_edit1 | Exactly one Damerau–Levenshtein edit, both folded symbols length ≥ 5. |

Real-image hashes cover 2692/2956 launches; specific-post references cover 1109/2956. Missing features contribute no vote. Votes are independently evaluated predicates, not mutually exclusive text strata; overlapping exact and fuzzy clues can double-count the same underlying evidence. Symbol equality and edit-distance-one are mutually exclusive, so all signals cannot fire together.

A single candidate/earlier-face pair must supply at least k votes; votes from different faces are never pooled. Standalone ties prefer more votes, then the original exact text tier, then the earliest room/face. In text-OR-k experiments, the original exact text tier precedes vote count, then the earliest room/face. SOL-depth ties cannot be reconstructed. New doors expose their real metadata faces to later launches; every correctness score is against the selected room’s root, so a mistaken merge can harm later routes. This is research policy, not a change to §5 or the on-chain floor.

A dash means undefined precision because no routes occur, not perfect precision. Additional routes count launches left as new rooms by text alone. Net recall change includes changed roots and downstream losses; it is not additional routes divided by the denominator. Full route assignments, matched face/mask, pessimistic estimates and label-coverage decompositions are in `consensus_calibration.json`.

At k=4, text OR k adds 6 routes and 0.0494 estimated recall points, but precision falls from 99.83% to 99.54%. At k=5, standalone precision is 100.00%, recall is 26.78%, and it adds 0 routes over text. The highest threshold is mechanically unreachable because symbol equality and edit-one cannot both be true.

## Pairwise co-errors versus independence

The frame is every earlier/later pair of the 2956 real launches: 4367490 pairs. Indexed enumeration examines 41713 potentially supported pairs; the 21252 pairs firing any signal are explicit. All other pairs have an implicit zero mask. Estimator-supported positive relationships outside the six signals are still included when computing the negative-pair frame. Conditioning only on the signal union would itself create selection correlations, so that is not the frame.

For each pair, negative weight w = 1 − p_same from the frozen text estimator. Total negative weight is 4348919.378627. On that frame, signal error counts are Σw·I(signal); simultaneous errors are Σw·I(a)·I(b). Independence predicts marginal_a × marginal_b / total_negative_weight. Lift is observed/predicted; phi is Pearson correlation of the two trigger indicators on that negative-weight frame. These fractional figures are assistant-estimator extrapolations, not newly human-labelled errors, causal proof, or independent Bernoulli trials.

The estimator shows positive association for 13/15 signal pairs. Some absence of co-errors is mechanical or definitional: equality and edit-one are mutually exclusive, and the identity-positive policy forces name+symbol joint wrong weight to zero. Neither is evidence that real semantic errors are independent.

Direct-D cross-check: 542 actual launch pairs from 92 distinct identity pairs carry an existing D label and are not overridden by the positive definition; 97 fire no tested signal. Only 2/10 computable signal-pair correlations in the direct-D frame show positive association. The image vote fires on 0 D-labelled launch pairs, so its correlations are undefined, not evidence of image safety. The positive direct-D pairings are name_equal + fuzzy_name, x_post + symbol_edit1. Thus the broad correlated-error hypothesis has partial support and substantial label-selection limits; it is not uniformly established by this sample.

## Crowded versus distinctive themes

Define each launch’s density as the maximum of its nonempty folded-symbol launch frequency and its name-token launch frequencies, using tokens of length at least four. Count distinct launch records, not repeated tokens inside one name. Crowded means density at or above the observed nearest-rank p75 cutoff, 30 launches; ties included. This yields 765 crowded and 2191 distinctive launches. Full-sample frequencies define a post-hoc diagnostic only; no future information affects routing. These are lexical density groups, not human narrative-theme labels.

## Recommendation and label dependency

Reject k-of-n for v1 at every tested threshold. High thresholds can reach perfect estimated precision by retaining an existing text-routed subset; that is not incremental recall. Lower thresholds add routes at a precision cost. The image-free variant does not rescue the rule. The independent social audit remains a separate negative recommendation because its semantic label coverage cannot establish the bar. This rejects the measured unweighted threshold design; it is not evidence about every possible weighted classifier or a future held-out sample.

Raw feature availability, equality/mask counts, route counts, theme-density frequencies and which roots change are label-independent conditional benchmark observations. Every semantic precision/recall estimate, expected-copy denominator, weighted co-error and crowded-group precision uses the identity/URI policy and assistant labels or their text-stratum extrapolations. The direct-D table still uses assistant labels; none have human review. Same-post equality is close to ground truth for the referenced post, not independent truth about irreversible narrative absorption; domains are weaker.

The review CSV lists root/candidate mint pairs requiring judgement, existing label/coverage source and affected policies. It does not create or silently load new labels. A future candidate needs independent root-level human review on held-out data and the missing ordered room-state histories before a production precision/recall claim. No new third match condition, tie tier, example route or on-chain change is justified. The existing matcher signature already covers the routing decision. The launcher never chooses the room/door; founder-share plumbing defaults to 0 bps (no founder payout in v1).

## Reproduce

```bash
python3 scripts/narrative/calibrate_consensus.py
python3 scripts/narrative/run_revision.py
```

The standalone experiment uses only the standard library and checked-in JSON/CSV. It verifies original metadata byte hashes against the image manifest, consumes recorded pHashes without fetching/decoding images, and regenerates this report and its document blocks.
